questions.question: In a queueing network where finished jobs can be sent back for rework, what does the visit ratio of a station measure?
options: The probability that a job visits the station at least once, so it always lies between 0 and 1.
The long-run fraction of its time in the network that a job spends at the station.
The mean number of times a job visits the station per reference unit, which can exceed one.
The mean number of jobs present at the station, counting the job in service.

questions.question: In an open network, $\gamma_i$ is the external arrival rate at station $i$, $|\boldsymbol{\gamma}|=\sum_j\gamma_j$, and $\lambda_i$ is the total arrival rate at station $i$ solving the traffic equations. How many times, on average, does a job entering the network visit station $i$?
A closed queueing network uses station 1 as reference station, and its visit ratios satisfy $V_1=1$ and $V_3=0.5$. What does $V_3=0.5$ tell us about station 3?
options: Station 3 is visited on average once for every two visits to station 1.
Half of the jobs in the network are at station 3 at any moment.
A job leaving station 1 goes straight to station 3 with probability 0.5.
Station 3 completes on average 0.5 jobs per unit of time.

questions.question: A closed network of $m$ stations has Markov routing: $P_{ij}$ is the probability that a job leaving station $i$ goes next to station $j$, and $V_i$ is the visit ratio of station $i$. Which equation expresses flow balance at station $j$?

In a closed network with reference station 1, station $i$ has visit ratio $V_i$, mean service time $\mathbb{E}[S_i]$ per visit and mean sojourn time $\mathbb{E}[J_i]$ per visit. What is the mean amount of work a job brings to the server of station $i$ per visit to station 1?

After each operation at a machine, an inspection sends the job back to the same machine with probability $0.3$, independently of earlier inspections; otherwise the job leaves. What is the mean number of visits a job pays to the machine?

An open network has three stations with external arrival rates $\boldsymbol{\gamma}=(4,2,0)$ jobs per hour, and the traffic equations give total arrival rates $\boldsymbol{\lambda}=(5,3,9)$ per hour. What is the visit ratio of station 3, the mean number of visits per job entering the network?

In a closed network with reference station 1 the visit ratios are $V_1=1$, $V_2=0.5$ and $V_3=1.5$, and at population $n$ the throughput of station 1 is $\mathrm{TH}_1(n)=2$ jobs per hour. What is the throughput $\mathrm{TH}_3(n)$ of station 3?

A closed network has four single-server stations with visit ratios $\boldsymbol{V}=(1,2,0.4,1.5)$ and mean service times $(\mathbb{E}[S_1],\ldots,\mathbb{E}[S_4])=(0.1,0.3,1.8,0.6)$ hours. Which station is the bottleneck that limits the throughput?

After each visit to a test station, a job is sent back to that station with probability $0.4$, independently of earlier visits, and otherwise moves on. Let $T$ be its number of visits to the station. What is $\mathbb{P}(T=3)$?

In a closed network every row of the routing matrix $\boldsymbol{P}$ sums to one, and every station can be reached from every other station. Why must the equations $\boldsymbol{V}=\boldsymbol{V}\boldsymbol{P}$ be supplemented by the condition $V_1=1$?
options: Any constant multiple of a solution is again a solution, so the equations fix $\boldsymbol{V}$ only up to a factor.
Without it the only solution is $\boldsymbol{V}=\boldsymbol{0}$, because $\boldsymbol{I}-\boldsymbol{P}$ is invertible here.
Station 1 is the bottleneck, so its visit ratio must be the largest and is set to one.
Jobs enter the network at station 1, and $V_1=1$ records one entry per job.

questions.question: A closed network with Markov routing and reference station 1 has its population raised from $n$ to $n+1$ jobs, while the routing probabilities and service times stay the same. What happens to the visit ratios $V_i$?
options: They all grow by the factor $(n+1)/n$, because more jobs make more visits.
The bottleneck's ratio grows, because jobs spend longer queueing there.
They change with $n$, because $V_i=\mathrm{TH}_i(n)/\mathrm{TH}_1(n)$ and the throughputs depend on $n$.
They stay the same, because they are determined by the routing probabilities alone.

questions.question: An open network with Markov routing has external arrival rates $\gamma_i$ and visit ratios $\lambda_i/|\boldsymbol{\gamma}|$, where the $\lambda_i$ solve the traffic equations. Every station is and remains stable. Which change can alter these visit ratios?
options: Multiplying every external arrival rate $\gamma_i$ by the same factor $c>0$.
Halving every mean service time, so that each station is less heavily loaded.
Moving part of the external arrivals from one entry station to another.
Replacing Poisson external arrivals by deterministic arrivals with the same rates.

questions.question: A closed network has three stations. A job leaving station 1 always goes to station 2; a job leaving station 2 goes to station 1 with probability $0.25$ and to station 3 with probability $0.75$; a job leaving station 3 always returns to station 2. With $V_1=1$, what are $(V_2,V_3)$?

In an open network with total external arrival rate $|\boldsymbol{\gamma}|=4$ jobs per hour, the traffic equations give $\boldsymbol{\lambda}=(5,2,3)$ per hour, and the mean sojourn times per visit are $\mathbb{E}[J_1]=0.8$, $\mathbb{E}[J_2]=1.5$ and $\mathbb{E}[J_3]=0.4$ hours. What is the mean time $\mathbb{E}[J]$ a job spends in the network?

Jobs arrive at a single machine at rate $\gamma=3$ per hour. After each operation, inspection sends the job back to the machine with probability $0.25$, independently; otherwise it leaves. Each operation takes on average $\mathbb{E}[S]=0.2$ hours. What is the load $\rho$ of the machine?

In a closed network with population $n$, visit ratios $V_i$ are first defined with station 1 as reference. The reference is then switched to station 2, which had $V_2=0.5$. Which statement about the effect of this switch is correct?
options: Every visit ratio doubles, the reference throughput is unchanged, and each $\mathrm{TH}_i(n)$ doubles as well.
No visit ratio changes, because the ratios depend on the routing matrix alone.
Every visit ratio doubles, the reference throughput halves, and each $\mathrm{TH}_i(n)$ stays the same.
Every visit ratio halves, the reference throughput doubles, and the bottleneck may move to another station.

questions.question: In an open network, station $i$ has visit ratio $\lambda_i/|\boldsymbol{\gamma}|=0.6$, the mean number of visits per entering job. Under which additional condition may one conclude that exactly 60% of entering jobs visit station $i$ at least once?
options: No extra condition is needed: a visit ratio below one is the probability of a visit.
Every station is stable, so that the traffic equations describe the actual flows.
External arrivals form a Poisson process, so that arriving jobs see time averages.
No job can visit station $i$ more than once, for example because no route leads back to it.

questions.question: A closed network of three single-server stations contains one job. Its visit ratios are $\boldsymbol{V}=(1,0.5,2)$ relative to station 1, and the mean service times are $(\mathbb{E}[S_1],\mathbb{E}[S_2],\mathbb{E}[S_3])=(0.4,1,0.3)$ hours. What is the throughput $\mathrm{TH}_1(1)$ of station 1?

Every job enters a line at station 1 and visits stations 1, 2 and 3 in that order. After station 3 an inspection sends it back to station 1 with probability $0.1$, back to station 2 with probability $0.2$, and otherwise lets it leave, independently each time. What is the visit ratio of station 1?
